operations.source_excerpt: [F6] If changing one independent coordinate changes a bounded measurable statistic by at most $1/n$, McDiarmid's inequality bounds its upper tail by $\exp(-2nt^2)$. [[thm-mcdiarmid-bounded-differences]]
operations.proposed_replacement: [F6] If changing one independent coordinate changes a bounded measurable statistic by at most $1/n$, McDiarmid's inequality bounds each of its upper and lower tails by $\exp(-2nt^2)$; the lower-tail bound follows by applying the upper-tail bound to the negative statistic. [[thm-mcdiarmid-bounded-differences]]

operations.source_excerpt: Apply [F6] to each statistic with failure probability $\delta/2$ and $t=\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/(2n)}$. Outside a set of probability at most $\delta$, both $Z(S)\le\mathbb EZ(S)+t$ and $\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)\le\mathbb E\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)+t$. Combining with step 4.1 yields $Z(S)\le2\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)+3t$.
operations.proposed_replacement: Apply the upper-tail bound [F6] to $Z$ and to $-\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)$, each with failure probability $\delta/2$ and $t=\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/(2n)}$. Outside a set of probability at most $\delta$, both $Z(S)\le\mathbb EZ(S)+t$ and $\mathbb E\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)\le\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)+t$. Combining with step 4.1 gives $Z(S)\le\mathbb EZ(S)+t\le2\mathbb E\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)+t\le2\widehat{\mathfrak R}_S(\mathcal L_\gamma)+3t$.
